title: First arrivals: First qualifying slip
summary: Keep the first occurrence of each distinct reading, preserving encounter order. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.
descriptionMd:
The reception stamp should acknowledge each visitor's tag only on its first arrival. Rafi needs the first qualifying slip while the courier waits at the door. Later matches must not jump ahead in the tray.

Keep the first occurrence of each distinct reading, preserving encounter order.

Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.

Implement firstArrivalsFirstQualifyingSlip(readings, k). Use k exactly where specified above.
unitIntro: Set membership. Keep the first occurrence of each distinct reading, preserving encounter order. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with set membership. What state describes the portion you have already processed?
Keep the first occurrence of each distinct reading, preserving encounter order. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.
